None of those match — tar spot has black raised spots, physoderma shows banding pattern with midrib spots, eyespot has circular lesions with halos, gray leaf spot has rectangular elongated lesions. All clearly different. Let me view more to reach 12 total.

All other candidates are clearly eliminated:
- Northern corn leaf blight: large cigar-shaped tan lesions
- Holcus spot: round white spots with brown margins
- Stewart's wilt: seedling wilting, no pustules
- Carbonum leaf spot: large oval lesions with concentric rings
- Anthracnose leaf spot: oval lesions with dark margins and setae

**Final analysis:**
- Test image: small, dense, circular-to-oval orange/cinnamon-red pustules concentrated on upper leaf surface
- Southern rust reference matches perfectly: same color (orange/cinnamon, not brick-red), same small size, same density, same upper-surface preference
- Common rust is clearly different: brick-red, larger, more elongated pustules on both leaf surfaces
